recognize_zh: H&E 切片中可見寬大、帶狀、壁薄且幾乎無分隔的淡染菌絲，呈不規則分枝並散布於壞死組織內，加上上排門牙牙齦的壞死潰瘍照片（inset），符合侵襲性毛黴菌病（mucormycosis）。
features: Broad, ribbon-like, thin-walled pale eosinophilic hyphae with few or no septa
Irregular, non-parallel branching and folded/twisted hyphal profiles
Hyphae infiltrating necrotic stroma with scattered inflammatory cells and nuclear debris
Adjacent strands of residual epithelium/tissue at the edges of the field
Clinical inset: necrotic ulceration of the upper gingiva adjacent to the incisors
describe_en: Section of oral (gingival) tissue stained with H&E shows necrotic stroma permeated by numerous broad, ribbon-like, thin-walled hyphae that are pauci-septate and branch irregularly, with a scattered mixed inflammatory infiltrate and karyorrhectic debris. No narrow, regularly septate, acute-angle branching hyphae are identified. The clinical inset shows a necrotic ulcer of the upper gingiva. Findings are consistent with invasive mucormycosis in an immunocompromised post-transplant patient; fungal culture or molecular identification is recommended for speciation.

ddx.vs: Aspergillus hyphae are narrow, uniform, and regularly septate with parallel walls and dichotomous acute-angle branching, unlike the broad, pauci-septate ribbons seen here.
Fusarium hyphae resemble Aspergillus (narrow, septate) and may show adventitial sporulation, and are distinguished by culture or PCR.
Candida shows budding yeasts with pseudohyphae showing constrictions rather than broad ribbon-like hyphae.
